solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

S023-01.notes: No unneeded words, short paragraphs = spare; ornate/digressive/effusive are opposites.

S023-02.notes: Bright bands that are easy to notice = conspicuous (aposematism).

S023-03.notes: Opening comma before blank pairs with comma after 'however'; interrupter inside a single clause, so no semicolon. A leaves comma unpaired; C/D put semicolon between subject and verb.

S023-04.notes: 'By the time it arrives' (future, 2031) requires future perfect.

S023-05.notes: Testing many materials -> final choice: 'Ultimately'. 'Instead' is a mild trap but nothing is being replaced/contrasted.

S023-06.notes: Only C mentions nearly complete + rarity, explaining why unusual.

S023-07.notes: Where everything is wet, lichen grows on all sides, so moisture rather than orientation is the limit. A/C unsupported; B contradicts.

flags: minor: choice B omits serial comma ('4 for biography and only 0.5') while the stems elsewhere use it; harmless
S023-08.notes: Claim has two parts (faster in every genre, smallest gap for poetry); only B covers both. Differences 3, 4, 0.5 correct.

S023-09.notes: Still wakes at 4:29 and watches bus leave 'without him' = routine persists. B overreaches; C/D contradicted (retired; alarm no longer set).

S023-10.notes: Possessive relative pronoun before noun 'performance': whose. 'who's' = who is; 'her' creates comma splice.
